CXC-R-DP-2.title: Rendering Target Is a Transport-Level Concern

properties.glyph-source: On EVERY platform, glyph rasterization is engine-owned and derives from the same Plex TTF bytes:
properties.family-mapping: any `sans-serif`/unknown family → Plex Sans; families containing mono/courier/consolas/menlo → Plex Mono. There is deliberately NO system-font fallback chain; glyphs Plex lacks are substituted at the backend seam (`fonts.GLYPH_SUBSTITUTIONS`: ⚠→!, ✗→×, ⛔→Ø) identically everywhere.
properties.verified: text conformance scenes (`text` atlas, `text_native` FreeType) 100.00% identical / max_delta 0 between macOS (arm64) and Raspberry Pi 5 (Linux/aarch64), 2026-07-06.
properties.change: "Font = IBM Plex Sans + IBM Plex Mono, AND desktop text rendering moved from native Skia text to engine-owned FreeType glyph rasterization (Skia blits engine-rendered coverage bitmaps)."
context_for_change: prior_state: "Spec said 'a clean sans-serif, rendered via Skia/Canvas text API'. M1 shipped fontconfig/CoreText MakeFromName lookup — macOS↔Linux text was not even face-identical. The M2 resolved-input assumed bundling one TTF loaded via Typeface.MakeFromFile would yield pixel identity."

reasoning: "Measured 2026-07-06: MakeFromFile with the identical Plex TTF still diverged ~8% of text pixels (max_delta 225) between macOS and RPi5 — skia-python delegates glyph SCALING to the platform scaler (CoreText on macOS, FreeType on Linux) and their AA coverage differs. Pixel-identical text therefore requires owning rasterization: freetype-py is pinned (2.13.2, wheel bundles libfreetype) and uses the exact generate_atlas.py settings, so desktop glyphs are byte-identical across OS/arch and design-identical to the CYD atlas."

rejected_alternative: "(a) Accept ~92% text identity and loosen the pixel gate — rejected, [CXC-R-C1] is a gate not a preference. (b) Extend the bitmap atlas to all desktop sizes — rejected: widgets use arbitrary/fractional sizes; nearest-neighbor atlas scaling degrades desktop text quality."
counter_argument: "Per-glyph image blits are slower than a Skia text blob, and dropping the platform shaper loses kerning/ligatures/complex scripts."

counter_response: "Glyph images cache per (face,size,char,color); measured frame budget held ≥55fps with live text on both platforms (330fps macOS / 59.5fps RPi kiosk loop). Skia's simple MakeFromString path did no shaping either — nothing was lost; IME/complex text was already deferred ([CXC-R-ENGINE-TEXT] Phase 3)."

invalidating_assumption: "That widget text stays simple-script LTR and freetype-py stays version-pinned across deploy targets. If complex-script shaping becomes a requirement, revisit with a shaping engine (HarfBuzz) rasterizing through the same FreeType path; if a platform can't run freetype-py, it needs the atlas mode."

implication: "All goldens re-baked once against Plex+FreeType (2026-07-06). Every future desktop backend inherits ft_text.py rather than its platform text API. The browser backend (M3) must either run the same rasterizer (Pyodide: freetype-py compiled to WASM) or blit pre-rendered glyphs — native canvas fillText would break the pixel gate."

properties.change: "M5 as-built (2026-07-07, classic CYD): config-driven boot is OPERATIONAL on hardware — generic firmware (cyd/src/main.cpp contains ZERO composition), config source of truth = bus_storage assets namespace `bus://assets/displays/<device_id>.compose.yaml` with `displays/default.compose.yaml` fallback; device_id = `cyd-` + last-3 MAC octets (printed at boot) unless DISPLAY_DEVICE_ID overrides. RATIFIED by David 2026-07-07 (bus-native asset addressing; reuses existing bus_storage, keyed per device)."
context_for_change: prior_state: "[CXC-R-BOOT-SEQUENCE] step 5 names `GET /api/v1/config/{uuid}`; bus_storage as deployed has no /config-by-uuid endpoint but a fully working nested-assets namespace."

reasoning: "The assets namespace already gives per-device addressing, PUT-to-update (drives [CXC-R-C10] re-poll), and the same fetch path as every other bus:// asset — one client code path on a heap-starved MCU. A default-config fallback makes a factory-fresh unit render SOMETHING and log its identity, so assigning its config is a bus_storage PUT, never a firmware touch."

rejected_alternative: "Add a bespoke /api/v1/config/{uuid} endpoint to bus_storage — deferred: it duplicates the asset GET with a second addressing scheme; revisit if per-device config wants server-side logic (templating, capability negotiation)."

invalidating_assumption: "That displays stay on the flat 192.0.2.x segment where bus_storage is IP-reachable (mDNS is unavailable to ESP32 here and .local will not cross the planned VLAN30/35 split — the firmware bakes the IP via wifi_config.h)."

implication: "As-built boot subset: WiFi -> splash w/ device id -> fetch -> yaml_min parse (bounded YAML subset, host-tested vs all 6 example configs) -> compose_scene build -> render -> touch registry -> 60s config re-poll (byte-compare -> live scene swap, verified on hardware). DEFERRED, logged not faked: MQTT namespace subscribe/publish (steps 3/4/11 — bindings/behaviors in configs log 'deferred, no bus on this tier'), bus discovery announce, doc:// assets, PSRAM asset cache. Acceptance measured 2026-07-07: C9 boot->rendered-frame 2.2-2.9 s typical (worst 14 s on slow WiFi assoc), touch from frame 1; C12 one binary rendered THREE different configs (gauge dashboard / fleet status board / dradis sprite scene) by asset swap alone; C10 live re-poll swap captured in logs."

CXC-BIND-PRINCIPLE.title: State on the Bus, Behavior in the Widget
CXC-BIND-PRINCIPLE.status: operational (2026-07-06) — verified end-to-end over real MQTT: an Intelligence peer publishing `ship/red_alert = on` (one bit) drives the engine-owned blink identically to any publisher (`tests/render/smoke_bind_intelligence_mqtt.py`, 4/4 vs mqtt-broker.local).

properties.definition: The bus carries semantic STATE (`red_alert = on`, published once); the widget owns the temporal PRESENTATION (blink at 2s). Animation frames are never streamed over the bus.
properties.key-insight: This is the ComposeBus state-engine philosophy (meaning on the bus, interpretation at the edge) extended from value to *presentation*. A widget's reaction is engine-owned, so it is consistent and pixel-verified across every backend, and an Intelligence drives it at intent altitude — it flips one bit; it does not micromanage frames.
properties.implication: The reactive vocabulary is finite and declarative. Computation that a declarative binding cannot express belongs in a bus workload ([CXC-BIND-BOUNDARY]), not in the config.
properties.status: operational (2026-07-06) — verified end-to-end over real MQTT: an Intelligence peer publishing `ship/red_alert = on` (one bit) drives the engine-owned blink identically to any publisher (`tests/render/smoke_bind_intelligence_mqtt.py`, 4/4 vs mqtt-broker.local).

CXC-BIND-ATTR.title: Any Attribute Binds to a Namespace

properties.definition: A widget attribute may take a literal, a namespace reference, or a binding object. The core bindable set: `visible`, `opacity`, `rotation` (degrees), `scale`, `color`, plus each widget's value attributes. `visible` shipped in M4; this generalizes the same mechanism to the transforms and the rest.
forms: object — `visible: {namespace: red_alert, when: on, invert: false}` ; `opacity: {namespace: dim, default: 1.0}`
properties.value-map: an optional declarative map (NOT an expression) may translate a state to a value — `color: {namespace: alert_level, map: {ok: green, warn: amber, crit: red}}`. Maps are literal lookups only; anything arithmetic is DSL territory ([CXC-BIND-BOUNDARY]).
properties.transform-note: `rotation`/`scale` require the engine transform ops — trivial on the Skia tier (`canvas.rotate`/`scale`); on the CYD a raster rotate is costly, so transform bindings degrade/precompute there (CYD is POC). `visible`/`opacity`/`color` are cheap on every tier.
properties.test: a namespace value change updates the bound attribute within one frame ([CXC-R-C4]).
properties.implemented: `render/engine/bindings.py` (extraction/coercion) + `render/engine/parser.py` (extraction runs BEFORE widget construction, so constructors only see literals) + `render/engine/runtime.py` (subscription wiring, one-frame apply via schedule_update). Transforms are Widget base attributes (`opacity`/`rotation`/`scale`), applied by the container draw pass (`engine/layout.draw_child`: rotate/scale about the rect center, opacity as a composing paint multiplier) — the zero-transform path costs nothing. Coercion is type-directed by the target attribute's current value (bool → match, tuple/color attrs → color spec parse, numeric → float, str → str). Bare-string namespace form applies to visible/opacity/rotation/scale; all attrs bind via the object form. Hit-testing of ROTATED widgets still uses the axis-aligned arranged rect (known limitation; acceptable for indicator-tier transforms).
properties.status: operational (2026-07-06) — tests/render/test_bind_behaviors.py C1/C8 + golden `bind_transform_literals`.

properties.definition: A document- or widget-scoped `variables:` block declares named values reusable in attributes/bindings/behavior params via `$name`. Substitution is at parse time; there is no runtime evaluation.
properties.forms: a variable is a literal (`alert_period: 2000`) or itself a namespace binding (`heading: {namespace: nav/heading_deg}`). `$name` resolves to the literal, or to the binding (propagating reactivity).
properties.test: `$alert_period` used in a behavior's `period_ms` resolves to its declared value at load; a variable bound to a namespace stays reactive.
properties.implemented: `bindings.substitute_variables` — runs in `parse_widget_tree` AFTER spec-14 component stamping (component bodies may use document variables). Exact-token form (`period_ms: $alert_period`) replaces with the variable's value of ANY type (a binding dict propagates reactivity); embedded form (`text: "$sensor temp"`) stringifies scalars in place; unknown `$name` is left as a literal (a `"$100 budget"` label survives). Widget-scoped `variables:` blocks merge over the document scope; variable definitions may reference outer variables.
properties.status: operational (2026-07-06) — test_bind_behaviors.py C4 (4 tests).

CXC-BIND-BEHAVIOR.title: Trigger → Engine-Owned Behavior → Target Attribute
CXC-BIND-BEHAVIOR.status: operational (2026-07-06) — full library (blink/pulse/ramp/ramp_color/rotate/animate/transition), all trigger kinds, lifecycle + last-declared-wins tested; goldens `bind_red_alert_{on,off}`, `bind_dradis_{idle,mid_sweep}`.

properties.definition: A widget's `behaviors:` list maps a bus-state trigger to a named, engine-owned temporal behavior applied to a target attribute, parameterized. Behaviors run on the engine animation loop ([CXC-R-ENGINE-ANIM]).
properties.lifecycle: a behavior is active while its trigger holds; on release, the target reverts to its base value (literal or bound). `blink`/`pulse`/`rotate` are continuous; `ramp`/`animate` are one-shot on the trigger edge.
properties.composition: multiple behaviors on one widget are allowed; conflicts on the same target resolve last-declared-wins (documented, deterministic).
properties.seed: `Button.led_behaviors` (blink_500ms/while_pressed) + `engine/animation.py` prove the pattern; this generalizes it to any widget/attribute.
properties.implemented: `render/engine/behaviors.py` (BehaviorEngine) — every behavior value is a PURE function of elapsed time since activation; activation defers its start timestamp to the first tick, so `RenderApp.render_frame_at(t)` (the new deterministic fixed-timestep sampling mode) reproduces frames byte-identically. The wall-clock `run()` loop ticks the engine beside the Animator; easing/interpolation are REUSED from `engine/animation.py`. Binding/behavior interplay: when an attribute binding writes a target a behavior currently holds, the engine's `notify_base_change` updates the revert-to base, so release lands on the live bound value, not a stale snapshot.
properties.status: operational (2026-07-06) — full library (blink/pulse/ramp/ramp_color/rotate/animate/transition), all trigger kinds, lifecycle + last-declared-wins tested; goldens `bind_red_alert_{on,off}`, `bind_dradis_{idle,mid_sweep}`.
properties.change: "Trigger `is:` and binding `when:` comparison is CANONICAL, not raw-string: YAML-1.1 booleans, the binary state engine's `1`/`0`, and string publishes collapse to on/off tokens before comparing (`bindings.canon`)."
context_for_change: prior_state: "The spec example `when: { namespace: red_alert, is: on }` and the M4 visible `when:` used exact string comparison."

reasoning: "Measured while building the demo .compose.yaml files: YAML 1.1 loads unquoted `is: on` as boolean True, so str-comparison against a peer's published string 'on' NEVER matches — the exact config shape this spec documents would silently do nothing. Canonicalizing ('on'/'true'/'yes'/'1'/True → on; 'off'/'false'/'no'/'0'/False → off) makes the documented config work however the bit was published, aligning the trigger with the binary state-engine vocabulary."

rejected_alternative: "Require authors to quote ('is: \"on\"') — rejected: a silent-failure footgun baked into the spec's own canonical example; the Composer binding editor cannot fix what humans hand-author."

invalidating_assumption: "That no application needs to distinguish the literal string 'on' from boolean true, or '1' from 1, in a trigger. If one does, an explicit `is_exact:` form can be added without breaking `is:`."
implication: "Non-binary values compare case-insensitively, whitespace-trimmed. `when:` visible bindings inherit the same rule."

CXC-BIND-BOUNDARY.title: What Is NOT In the Config

properties.decision: **No arbitrary inline code** (e.g. inline Python) in `.compose.yaml`.
properties.rationale: it breaks define-once (Python can't run on the CYD/C++ or a TS-browser backend) and is an RCE surface on a fetch-from-bus display fleet. ESPHome's inline-C++ works only because it compiles to ONE runtime; ComposeUX is define-once-render-many.
properties.escape-hatch: real computation lives in a **bus workload** — a process that computes and publishes a namespace, which a widget then binds. Compute where it belongs; the config stays declarative and portable.
properties.deferred: a **sandboxed, restricted expression DSL** (HA-Jinja-flavored: arithmetic, `ns()` lookups, conditionals; interpretable identically on Python AND CYD/JS) is the sanctioned middle ground for the last ~10%, but it is a separate, **use-case-gated** deliverable ([CXC-RM-BEHAVIORS]) — collect ~5 real high-need cases first. This spec is the declarative 90%.
properties.implemented: `bindings.strip_code_fields` removes code-shaped keys (code/script/python/eval/exec/expr/template/lambda/js/…) from every widget spec and behavior entry at parse time, with a logged [CXC-BIND-BOUNDARY] warning; `bindings.validate_map` refuses maps that are non-dicts or carry template/expression-shaped strings (`{{…}}`, `${…}`, leading `=`) — the whole binding is dropped, the attribute keeps its literal. Verified with an import-side-effect canary: the payload file is never created (test_c7).
properties.status: operational (2026-07-06).

CXC-LOT-INTENT.title: Vector Motion Without Frames on the Bus
CXC-LOT-INTENT.status: OPERATIONAL on the Skia tier (2026-07-07) — `render/widgets/lottie.py` + `render/lottie/` package; C1–C5, C7 PASS; C6 (CYD sprite sheet) deferred to M5. NOTE the renderer-seam change record below: skottie is NOT bound by skia-python, so the Skia tier currently renders via the engine's Canvas-contract Lottie evaluator (Skia still rasterizes every pixel).

properties.definition: The LottieWidget plays a vector animation defined by a Lottie JSON document. Its use is non-interactive motion — a dradis sweep, a pulsing alert glyph, a spinner, a transition flourish.
properties.key-insight: Lottie is the *pure-Skia* animation primitive — **skottie** is Skia's own Lottie renderer, so it composites through the same backend as everything else and needs no external decoder (contrast [CXC-RM-MEDIA], which does). Playback is driven by bus state, never by streaming frames.
properties.status: OPERATIONAL on the Skia tier (2026-07-07) — `render/widgets/lottie.py` + `render/lottie/` package; C1–C5, C7 PASS; C6 (CYD sprite sheet) deferred to M5. NOTE the renderer-seam change record below: skottie is NOT bound by skia-python, so the Skia tier currently renders via the engine's Canvas-contract Lottie evaluator (Skia still rasterizes every pixel).

properties.browser: **skottie ships inside CanvasKit** — so under Decision 1 Option A (Pyodide + CanvasKit) the browser plays the same animation nearly for free; a TS re-port would need lottie-web instead (a point for Option A).
properties.test: the same Lottie at the same logical time renders design-identically on the Skia tier and (as sprite frames) on the CYD.

properties.constraint: like state-driven behaviors ([SPEC:CXC-BIND]), Lottie playback is time-based; for pixel-goldens it must sample deterministically — render the animation at a fixed logical time (reuse `RenderApp.render_frame_at(t)`), so golden frames reproduce byte-identically macOS↔RPi.

properties.role: The player exposes a control surface that binds to namespaces/variables via the [SPEC:CXC-BIND] mechanism — the same "state on the bus, behavior in the widget" model, applied to animation transport.
properties.dradis: the sweep is a Lottie whose `speed` (or `goToAndStop` progress) is bound to a `scanning`/heading namespace — the needle position is bus-driven, the interpolation is engine-owned.
properties.test: publishing to the bound `speed` namespace changes playback rate within one frame; `goToAndStop` bound to a value holds the matching frame; `playSegments` loops the named range.

CXC-LOT-ASSET.title: Lottie Source Is a Bus Asset

properties.role: the animation JSON is referenced as `src: doc://…/x.json` or `bus://assets/…/x.json`, fetched via the asset manager (`render/engine/assets.py`) with caching. Embedded images inside the Lottie resolve through the same asset path.

`composeio push` pre-renders the Lottie (via skottie, offline) into a **sprite sheet** stored in document_store ([CXC-R-C18]); the CYD firmware plays the frame sequence. Frame count/size are bounded for the ESP32 (PSRAM budget); a `fps`/`frames` cap is declared per animation.
properties.degradation: bound playback controls that the sprite-sheet can honor (play/pause/loop, goToAndStop to a baked frame) work; continuous `setSpeed` maps to nearest baked frame rate. Segment/marker playback maps to baked frame ranges.

CXC-SVG-INTENT.title: Decompose SVG to the Drawing Contract

properties.definition: The engine includes a platform-independent SVG parser that converts an SVG document into `Canvas` primitive calls (paths, rects, circles, text, fills, strokes, gradients, transforms, clips). The Canvas backend then draws them like anything else.
properties.key-insight: Because SVG decomposes to the *existing* Canvas contract, it renders on every backend for free — Skia (crisp), CanvasKit (browser), and the CYD (subject to its primitive subset). Crisp vector text (a stylized "Red Alert") and every diagram tool become universally renderable.
properties.status: planned

properties.definition: a platform-independent parser (Python, shared) maps SVG elements to Canvas calls per the [CXC-R-DRAW-SVG] table:
properties.attributes: `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `opacity`, `transform` (translate/rotate/scale/matrix) map to style + transform state. (`transform` uses the transform ops added for [SPEC:CXC-BIND].)
properties.coverage: the above element + attribute set is the conformance target ([CXC-R-C14]); unsupported features degrade to a warning, not a crash.
properties.test: a reference SVG exercising every mapped element renders correctly and pixel-identically macOS↔RPi.

properties.role: Skia/CanvasKit render the full mapping. The CYD's `ESP32Canvas` implements a primitive *subset* (no fill_arc/paths/transforms yet — M5), so complex SVG (arbitrary paths, gradients, transforms) degrades on the CYD until M5 fills those primitives; simple SVG (rects/circles/lines/text) renders now.
properties.test: a simple SVG renders on the CYD; a path-heavy SVG is flagged as degraded, not crashed.

properties.role: an `SvgWidget` renders an SVG referenced as `src: doc://…/x.svg` or `bus://assets/…/x.svg` (asset manager, cached), scaled to its rect (fit modes as Image). A bound `src` swaps the graphic reactively ([SPEC:CXC-BIND]).

properties.flow: diagram text (in `.compose.yaml` or a referenced doc) → a **diagram service** (hub workload running Mermaid.js/Graphviz in Node) renders it to SVG → the SVG is stored in document_store → an SvgWidget references `doc://diagrams/{id}.svg` and renders it. When the diagram source changes, the service re-renders and the widget updates (config poll or bus event).
properties.role: the diagram service is a simple hub workload — it watches for diagram text in bus_storage, renders, stores. This is the [CXC-R-C15] pipeline.

CXC-GEST-INTENT.title: The One Gesture the Displays Need

properties.definition: recognize a directional flick (up/down/left/right) from a single-touch down→move→up sequence and publish it. No multitouch, no pinch, no rotate (deliberately out of scope) — those add cost the display fleet doesn't need.
properties.rationale: touch displays (the CYD's XPT2046 resistive panel; touch monitors on RPi/MinnowBoard) want swipe navigation — flip a tab, dismiss a dialog, page a list. Single-touch keeps recognition cheap enough for the constrained tier.
properties.status: planned

properties.definition: on a pointer/touch down→move→up, classify a swipe when the travel exceeds `min_distance` within `max_time` and the path is dominantly axial; the direction is the dominant axis + sign. Otherwise the sequence remains a tap/long-press/pan (existing M1 behavior — swipe recognition must not regress those).
properties.backends: pointer/touch events already reach the engine (SDL on desktop, XPT2046 on CYD). Swipe classification is Layer-2 (shared), so it works on every backend that delivers pointer events.
properties.test: a down→right-move→up over threshold yields `right`; a slow short drag yields pan, not swipe; each of the four directions classifies correctly.

CXC-GEST-BUS.title: A Swipe Is a Bus Event

properties.definition: a recognized swipe publishes an interaction event — a namespace carrying the direction (and target widget id / position). Widgets or apps subscribe and react; nothing is hardwired in the engine.
properties.intelligence-parity: because the swipe is a published event and the engine also accepts injected interaction events, an Intelligence publishing a swipe drives the surface identically to a finger — the credo ([CXC-R-CONTROL]).
properties.test: a swipe in each direction publishes the correct event; a config that maps swipe-left to a tab change switches tabs; an Intelligence-injected swipe produces the identical reaction.

CXC-HW-INTENT.title: Logic Without a Screen, and Without Python
CXC-HW-INTENT.status: planned (spec) — build gated on the headless runtime + the expression DSL ([CXC-HW-DSL]).

properties.definition: A headless widget is a ComposeUX widget with no render — it consumes and produces namespace values on the bus using the same state engines, bindings, and behaviors as a visual widget. For most logic (state that evolves over time, conditional rates, thresholds, derived values) it replaces writing a Python bus workload.
properties.key-insight: it decouples *logic* from *devices*. The logic runs headless anywhere (hub / Pi / laptop); you only need an ESP32 when you want to bind a *physical* sensor or peripheral to a namespace — the silicon's job shrinks to "map signals ↔ peripherals." You can emulate a whole system in headless YAML and bind reality in incrementally.
properties.status: planned (spec) — build gated on the headless runtime + the expression DSL ([CXC-HW-DSL]).

CXC-HW-MODEL.title: Same Unit as a Visual Widget, Minus the Render

properties.definition: a headless widget is state (namespaces + engines) + bindings (subscribe/publish) + behaviors (temporal/conditional), authored in `.compose.yaml`, with no draw. It composes on the bus via pub/sub — decoupled, like every ComposeIO participant: it publishes/subscribes namespaces and never holds a reference to another widget.
properties.implication: a headless fuel_tank and a visual gauge are the *same kind of thing* — one renders, one doesn't. The whole system is a graph of headless (logic) + visual (presentation) widgets on one bus, one model, one engine, Intelligence-drivable as peers.

CXC-HW-DSL.title: Arithmetic Goes Through the Expression DSL

properties.constraint: headless logic needs computation — `remaining -= rate·dt`, the pump's conditional rate, `readiness = fuel≥X and charge≥Y`. The declarative behaviors cover much of it (ramp, conditions), but genuine arithmetic/derived values are the sandboxed-expression-DSL boundary ([CXC-RM-BEHAVIORS], use-case-gated).
properties.key-insight: **headless widgets don't just need the DSL — they define it.** Designing a handful of real headless widgets produces exactly the 5 gating use-cases, from need rather than speculation. This spec and the DSL advance together.

properties.definition: headless widgets run on a **headless ComposeUX runtime** — the engine minus the rendering backend — that loads their `.compose.yaml`, connects to the bus, and executes them under a declared schedule. It runs wherever is convenient (the hub, a Pi, a container); it is not tied to a display.
properties.change: "Deploy source is bus_storage on the display-boot pattern (roster + per-widget config), NOT document_store."
context_for_change: prior_state: "Open question framed as: push the headless widget to document_store, and config the runtime to fetch named widgets from document_store."

reasoning: "The visual tier already solves this: a display fetches `bus://assets/displays/<device_id>.compose.yaml` from bus_storage ([CXC-R-BOOT]). A headless widget IS a `.compose.yaml`; a runtime is a display's logic-tier peer. Using bus_storage on the same pattern makes the two tiers mirror images (one loader, one addressing scheme, one fungible-identity story) instead of parallel inventions. `bus://assets/` is the config/asset store; `doc://` is for structured JSON records — the config belongs in the former."

rejected_alternative: "document_store as the definition source — rejected: it splits the deploy model from the already-working display path and puts a config asset in the record store. document_store is retained for the orthogonal job of persisting a widget's runtime OUTPUT, not its definition."

invalidating_assumption: "That headless configs never need document_store's versioning/query over bus_storage's asset semantics. If they do, the roster can point at `doc://` refs without changing the loader contract."
implication: "A runtime needs one indirection a display doesn't — the roster — because it hosts many widgets where a display renders one config."

properties.definition: each headless widget declares how it runs. Three modes, matched to how logic actually behaves:
properties.note: these mirror the serverless scheduling triad (daemon / cron / event) but are bus-native — the trigger is a ComposeBus observation, and the runtime can host many widgets across all three modes.
properties.test: a continuous widget updates its output every tick; a periodic widget fires on its interval; a bus-triggered widget executes only when its trigger namespace publishes.

properties.key-insight: a headless widget is **not a new execution model** — it is the engine's existing per-frame evaluation with the *draw step removed and the clock source swapped*. The visual loop is `advance behaviors at t → re-evaluate bindings → draw`; headless is `advance behaviors at t → re-evaluate bindings → publish changed outputs`. Same core, null rendering backend. This is the literal proof of "engine minus backend."

properties.verdict: this is not a re-creation of Node-RED. There is real overlap at the *surface* — a node/flow editor, scheduled/triggered logic, bus messaging — but the core model differs enough to be complementary, not competitive.
properties.interop: both speak MQTT, so they bridge cleanly — a ComposeUX widget (headless or visual) emits a namespace → MQTT → a Node-RED flow reacts, and vice versa. That's a feature (great for Node-RED fans), not a seam to close.

properties.role: Composer's Flow mode ([SPEC:CXC-FLOW], realized in [SPEC:CXC-FLAUTH]) is the authoring surface — a headless widget is a logic node in the same graph as visual widgets and namespace hubs (the Flow-mode node model is being kept non-visual-friendly for exactly this). Authoring, wiring, and scheduling a headless widget happen in the same tool as the displays it feeds.

CXC-DSL-INTENT.title: Close the Six Harvested Gaps, Open No Code Surface

properties.definition: a restricted, sandboxed expression language usable anywhere a `.compose.yaml` today takes a literal or a single namespace reference. It computes a value from bus namespaces, inline variables, and tick context (`dt`, `t`) using arithmetic, comparisons, booleans, a ternary, and a closed set of functions — nothing else.
properties.origin: this is NOT speculative. Its entire scope is the six use-cases HARVESTED empirically from building the jump-drive triad declaratively in Headless Widgets Pass 1 ([CXC-RM-BEHAVIORS] dsl-gate-MET; `~/.composeio/dsl_candidates.jsonl`, source `headless-pass1`). The DSL exists to close exactly these and no more:

CXC-DSL-GRAMMAR.title: A Bare Typed Expression, Not a Template

properties.form: a single expression that evaluates to one value (number / bool / string). No statements, no assignment, no blocks, no interpolation braces. It lives in an explicit `expr:` field (opt-in — see [CXC-DSL-SITES]), so a bare literal field is never silently reinterpreted.

CXC-DSL-SEMANTICS.title: One Numeric Model, No Surprises, No NaN on a Gauge

properties.change: "Non-finite function/modulo inputs return IEEE results (matching the C++ backend), never raise — the evaluator is now total."
context_for_change: prior_state: "`round/floor/ceil(1e400)` raised `OverflowError` and `1e400 % 2` raised `ValueError` from `math.fmod` — uncaught, outside the value|error contract; the corpus never pinned non-finite fn/mod args, so Pass-2 conformance passed anyway."

reasoning: "Found by the Pass-2b falsification test — the FIRST independent re-implementation (C++/CYD) exposed it: Fable's C++ was total by construction, and a 30k-expression differential fuzz vs the reference hit 175 crash cases. An overflowing expression must degrade, not crash a display; totalizing to IEEE is consistent with the existing guarded-div philosophy and keeps Python matching the already-total C++. This is exactly the latent-Pythonism that 2b-first was sequenced to surface ([CXC-DSL-CROSSPLAT])."

rejected_alternative: "Make it a `DslEvalError` — rejected: less useful than a total IEEE result and would force the C++ to also raise; totality is the lower-friction agreement point and matches guarded-div."

invalidating_assumption: "That NaN *bit* parity holds on the ESP32 soft-float. It is UNVERIFIED, so only deterministic (inf/finite) totality cases are corpus-pinned (`totality` group, 8 cases); NaN-producing cases (`1e400 % 2`) are deliberately NOT pinned."
implication: "Corpus grew 226→234; Python reference + native C++ both 234/234; on-device remains 226/226 proven (the +8 are universal IEEE bits on the identical C++ interpreter)."

properties.decision: the DSL is **stateless** — it has no assignable variables and no memory between evaluations. The one use-case that looks stateful (variable-rate integration, #1) is expressed as an **output expression that reads its own current namespace**: `outputs: [{namespace: fuel/remaining, expr: "ns('fuel/remaining') - ns('pump/flow_rate') * dt"}]`. Each `tick(t)` reads the current value, computes the next, publishes; the next tick reads that. The bus IS the state; the expression stays a pure function.
properties.why: keeping the language pure (no assignment, no loops, no accumulators) is what makes it (a) trivially sandboxable, (b) deterministic under the [CXC-HW-RUNTIME] explicit-time `tick(t)` — golden `tick(0.0), tick(0.1)…` reproduces the exact integrated sequence, and (c) portable — an assignment/scope model would be far harder to make bit-identical on C++/JS.

CXC-DSL-CROSSPLAT.title: The Conformance Corpus IS the Contract

properties.principle: the DSL is only define-once if `expr` yields the **same bits** on CPython, C++/ESP32, and (future) JS. That guarantee is not asserted in prose — it is an **executable shared conformance corpus**: a set of `{expr, ns_values, vars, dt, t → expected_value}` cases that EVERY backend interpreter must reproduce exactly. This is the [CXC-R-C1] golden-frame discipline applied to expression evaluation instead of pixels.

CXC-DSL-SANDBOX.title: Why This Is Not Arbitrary Code ([CXC-BIND-BOUNDARY] upheld)

properties.deliverable: re-author `render/examples/headless/widgets/{fuel_tank,fuel_pump,jump_engine}.compose.yaml` to USE `expr:` — real variable-rate drain, real conditional pump rate, single-expression readiness AND — collapsing the Pass-1 3-widget/2-namespace/2-hop workaround. This closes [CXC-HW] compliance **C2** (full jump-drive from fuel+charge arithmetic) which Pass 1 could only satisfy partially, WITHOUT violating C8.

properties.reasoning: David will *rarely* use the default look (e.g. BSG progress bars need a bespoke, consistent feel) — so the default's value is being **inspectable and forkable**. A component is an author-readable `.compose.yaml` composition you clone and restyle; a code widget hides its rendering in Python/C++ and locks the look. Composites also render on every backend for free (they compose primitives that already implement the Canvas contract) and reuse the binding/DSL/component systems already built.
properties.consequence: the "default implementation" IS the deliverable artifact — seeing it is the point. Custom variants are forks that keep the shared tokens ([CXC-PRIM-TOKENS]) for family consistency and change the rest.
properties.note: existing code widgets that overlap (`power_toggle` ≈ switch, `checkbox`, `tab`) are NOT retired; these composites are the forkable family beside them.

CXC-PRIM-TOKENS.title: The Shared Token Set (ratified from the pre-vis, David 2026-07-09)

properties.surfaces: card/panel over an inset track; cool-biased neutrals.
properties.conventions: corner radius **4px**; thumbs are pill/circular; tracks **6–10px**; value labels in **mono**; both light+dark themed.
properties.rule: a fork keeps these tokens for a consistent family and restyles the rest. The tokens are the contract that makes bespoke variants still look related.

properties.gap: the engine already delivers `on_pan_start/on_pan/on_pan_end` to widgets ([CXC-RM-M1]) and publishes tap/long_press interactions, but there is no primitive that converts a drag into a **normalized value published to a namespace**.
properties.contract: a small, reusable interaction behavior — a draggable region maps pointer position along its axis to a `[min,max]` value (respecting `step`) and publishes it to a namespace. Modes: **live** (publish on every `on_pan`) or **on_release** (publish once on `on_pan_end`). Deterministic + bus-native: an Intelligence can "drag" by publishing the value directly, identical to a finger.
properties.reuse: this is the same "state on the bus, behavior in the widget" model; the slider's thumb position is a normal bound expression on the published value, so the visual is pure composite — only the *input* (pan→publish) is the new seam.

CXC-PRIM-REPEAT.title: The `repeat` Generator (the segment_bar needs this; keyboard/numpad want it)

properties.gap: the component expander ([14-composer-components]) substitutes `{{param}}` into a FIXED template — it cannot emit a *variable* number of children from a count param. An N-segment bargraph, and cleanly-generated key grids, need "clone this child N times, indexed."
properties.decision: build a **code widget for this? NO** — that would be the first primitive to break define-once (needing a separate C++/CYD implementation) and would lock the look. Instead add a minimal **`repeat` construct** to the expander: a child carrying `repeat: <count> as: <name>` is unrolled at load into `count` concrete children, substituting the integer index token (`{{i}}`) 0..count-1 (and `{{count}}`). Nothing more — no load-time arithmetic engine.
properties.reuse: `repeat` generalizes — keyboard/numpad key grids become generated rows rather than hand-listed (a follow-on refactor, not required now); tick marks, gauge ticks, any repeating structure.
properties.composition: `repeat` runs in the same load-time expansion pass as `{{param}}`/`use:`; nested `repeat` and `repeat` inside a `use:` component must compose. Layout keys ([14] `_LAYOUT_KEYS`) on the repeated child apply per-copy so the container lays them out (a horizontal/vertical row of segments).

properties.gap: dropdown needs a transient overlay list with select + outside-dismiss. Overlay mechanics already exist (the Command arm-confirm + BusMonitor pop-out use `DialogWidget`); what's missing is a **list-select popup** as a reusable interaction.
properties.contract: a popup surface anchored to the field, rendering an item list; an item tap publishes the selected value to a namespace and dismisses; an outside tap / escape dismisses without change. Reuse the existing dialog/overlay layer rather than inventing a second overlay system.

CXC-AUDIO-INTENT.title: Sound Is an Output Peripheral, Parallel to the Display

properties.definition: a ComposeUX surface (headed or headless) can emit audio in response to bus state. The unit declares a **sound intent bound to a trigger** ("play `alarm` while `ship/red_alert` is on"); the platform's audio backend performs it. The config never carries audio samples — it carries the *intent*, exactly as it carries drawing intent, not pixels.
properties.key-insight: this is the **Canvas-contract pattern applied to audio**. Just as "own every pixel" gave a ~30-fn Canvas contract implemented per display backend, audio gives a small **Audio contract** implemented per audio backend. The widget/config is backend-agnostic; portability is by construction.

properties.insight: audio is an output the way pixels are — so a **headless** widget can play sound. A bus-triggered headless widget sounds an alarm when `jumpdrive/readiness` flips; a **sound-only ESP32** (a DFPlayer + no screen) is a headless ComposeUX node whose *peripheral is audio instead of pixels*. This is [CXC-HW-INTENT] taken at its word — "the silicon's job shrinks to map signals ↔ peripherals," and a speaker is just another peripheral.
properties.consequence: the audio capability lives at the widget/runtime layer, not the render layer, so it is available on the headless runtime and on visual surfaces alike.

CXC-AUDIO-CONTRACT.title: The Audio Contract (intent set — to be bounded)

properties.definition: a small, closed set of audio intents a backend implements — the audio analog of the Canvas contract. Candidate set (to ratify):
properties.discipline: like the DSL and the Canvas contract, the set is CLOSED and small so it's realizable on a $3 MCU and a Pi alike; growth is a spec change, not an author liberty.

properties.model: a sound is bound to a trigger the same way a behavior is ([CXC-BIND]) — `when ship/red_alert is on → loop play_clip('alarm')`; release stops it. Bus-native and Intelligence-drivable: an Intelligence "sounds the alarm" by publishing one bus bit, identical to any other actor. Determinism where it matters (a bus-triggered headless sound fires on the observed publish, [CXC-HW-SCHEDULE]).

CXC-NFC-INTENT.title: An NFC Reader Is an Input Peripheral

properties.definition: a device with an NFC reader observes tags and **publishes a semantic namespace** on tag arrival/departure. The config declares the reader → namespace mapping; the platform's NFC backend performs the read. This is [CXC-HW-INTENT] on the input side — "the silicon's job shrinks to map signals ↔ peripherals," and a tag reader is just another peripheral producing a signal.
properties.symmetry: NFC is the **input dual of the audio actuator** ([SPEC:CXC-AUDIO]). Together they name a pattern ([CXC-NFC-PATTERN]): ComposeUX nodes bind *input* peripherals (touch, NFC, lure sensors) that publish and *output* peripherals (display, audio) that actuate — all namespace-scoped, all board-profile facts.

properties.shape: a tag event carries **presence** (binary: present / removed), **uid** (the tag's id), and optionally a **payload** (decoded NDEF text/URL/records, json). A reader publishes these to its declared namespace(s) — e.g. `access/badge` (uid + presence) and optionally `access/badge_data` (payload).
properties.pattern-ready: uid namespaces work with `subscribe_pattern` ([SPEC:CXC-PATSUB]) — many readers under `access/*` are one subscription.

CXC-NFC-SCOPE.title: Internal vs Bus Is Just Namespace Scope

properties.decision: "emit internal to the widget" and "push to the ComposeBus" are NOT two mechanisms — both are a namespace publish; the difference is **scope**. A **local/design-scoped** namespace stays within the surface (a tag flips a widget's state via an ordinary binding/behavior); a **global/external** namespace ([CXC-FL-DISCOVERY] `external`) is visible to other bus participants. Same publish, different reach — the author picks the scope.
properties.consequence: a headed widget can react to a tag locally (tap-to-scan-style), a headless widget can turn a tag into a shared event, and an Intelligence sees tag events like any other bus traffic.

CXC-NFC-TRANSPORT.title: The Reader Is a Board-Profile Fact

properties.definition: which NFC reader a device has — PN532 / RC522 / ST25R over **I2C / SPI / UART** on an MCU (the Class-B lure's I2C/serial is literally this transport), or a USB / PC-SC reader on a Pi / MinnowBoard / desktop — is declared in the board profile ([CXC-RM-M5] `board_profile.h`), exactly like the display driver and the audio backend. The same config runs on whatever reader is wired.

properties.observation: with touch (input), NFC (input), the lure sensors (input), display (output), and audio (output), a general shape is now visible — **a ComposeUX node binds physical peripherals to namespaces; inputs publish, outputs actuate, all scoped local or bus, all board-profile facts.** NFC is the first *explicit input-peripheral spec beyond touch*.
properties.note: PROMOTED (2026-07-10) — the generalization is now **[SPEC:CXC-HAL]** (the tiered Peripheral HAL): NFC is a Tier-2 (reusable-driver bus peripheral) citizen of it. Reed switch = Tier 1 (declarative), R503 fingerprint = Tier 3 (direct integration).

properties.problem: today, wiring a physical sensor to a namespace means writing code. That makes "bind reality in incrementally" ([CXC-HW-INTENT]) expensive for the *common* case — a reed switch, a PIR, a pot — which is 90% of real sensors.
properties.definition: a tiered Hardware Abstraction Layer that binds physical peripherals to ComposeBus namespaces, so the common sensor is a **declarative descriptor** (config-only) and only genuinely stateful devices need code. It is the input-side dual + generalization of the output actuator backends (Canvas/display, Audio) and the promotion of [CXC-NFC-PATTERN].
properties.payoff: emulate a whole system in headless YAML, then bind a reed switch to `door/state` by adding a descriptor line — not a driver.

CXC-HAL-FACE.title: The Boundary Is Per-Interaction-Face, Not Per-Device

properties.insight: a device can straddle. The R503's **runtime face** — "scan → matched id → publish" — is HAL-shaped (it looks exactly like NFC, Tier 2). Its **management face** — enroll / delete / manage templates — is Tier 3. So a device may expose a **declarative HAL face for its steady-state read AND a direct-integration face for its operations**. The seam runs through the device, not around it.
properties.consequence: don't ask "is this a HAL device?"; ask "which of its *interactions* are value/event (HAL) vs. operations (direct)?" — and wire each accordingly.

properties.semantics: the state **engine** (binary / tri_level / continuous_0_255 / enum / json) + the **value-map** ([CXC-BIND-C8]) turn a raw read into meaning, uniformly across all tiers.

CXC-HAL-DEVICE.title: The Device's Local Bus Is First-Class; Sensing and Emit-Scope Are Orthogonal to Headed/Headless (David 2026-07-10)

properties.correction: reading a sensor does NOT imply headless, and emitting does NOT imply the shared bus. The CYD is the counterfactual — a **headed** device (it renders) that ALSO reads peripherals (its 4-pin JST connectors). Two orthogonal axes, both hanging off the device's **local bus**:

CXC-HAL-TOPOLOGY.title: First-Class vs Relayed — Same Semantic Contract, Different Topology (David 2026-07-10)

properties.concept: a device participates in ComposeBus in one of two **topologies**, with the SAME semantic contract (the namespaces it emits/consumes). Orthogonal to the HAL tier and to headed/headless:

CXC-HAL-ACTUATE.title: Output Actuators Mirror Input Sensors — "Define Once, Actuate Many" (David 2026-07-10, grounded in 3 real boards)

properties.symmetry: the HAL has a symmetric OUTPUT side, not just display + audio. Input Tier 1 = read GPIO/ADC → publish a namespace; **Output Tier 1 = subscribe a namespace → drive GPIO/PWM/relay/low-side-switch**. Input Tier 2 = a bus-register sensor via a driver; **Output Tier 2 = a physical actuator via a driver** (an H-bridge / motor controller / shift register). Display (the Canvas contract) and audio ([SPEC:CXC-AUDIO]) are the rich, special-cased actuators; simple physical actuators (lights, relays, motors) are the Tier-1/2 output HAL.

CXC-ER-INTENT.title: Make the MCU a Live Node

properties.definition: build the reactive engine in C++ for the MCU — an **on-device bus client** (MQTT now; CAN later, [CXC-PS-CAN]) + a **namespace store** + the **binding/behavior engine** (the Python `[SPEC:CXC-BIND]`/`[CXC-HEADLESS]` model ported) + the **on-chip DSL** (2b, `cyd/src/dsl.{h,cpp}`, already proven on ESP32). A bus value now *drives* something on-device instead of being ignored.
properties.foundation: `firmware/esp32_mqtt_client/` (an ESP32-C3 MQTT ComposeBus client — WiFi + PubSubClient) + the portable DSL — R1 wires these together.

properties.definition: one C++ core, independent of display/board: bus client → namespace store → on value-change, re-evaluate the bindings/behaviors that read that namespace (calling the DSL for `expr:`), then apply the result to an **output** — a widget attribute (display boards), a physical actuator (HAL), or a published derived namespace (headless logic). Headless-capable by construction (no render dependency), exactly like the Python `RenderApp(headless=True)`.

CXC-ER-BOARDS.title: One Core, Three Variants (the abstraction shake-out)

CXC-ER-DEVICE.title: The Device Model (local bus + bridge policy)

properties.definition: a headless-authored display widget for the reactive-render tier ([CXC-ER-RENDER], lands on the R5 Qualia surface): it subscribes to a contact array on the bus and re-renders the scope on change. The narrow waist is the bus contract ([CXC-ER-DRADIS-BUS]) — the `dradis_contacts` widget and the scenario driver (a bus peer that spawns/moves contacts) each lower to THAT, never to each other.
properties.key-insight: this is [CXC-BIND-PRINCIPLE] ("state on the bus, behavior in the widget") realized end-to-end on a non-trivial widget: position/allegiance/alert-bit are semantic state on the bus; projection, motion heading, blink phase, and counts are all widget-owned. The demo's "reactive" is exactly the behavior the widget owns.
properties.own-ship: the Battlestar (own-ship) is NOT a contact — it is a static center `image` widget in the scene. Contact/threat counts are DERIVED by the widget from the array, never published separately ([DP-CIO-3] pushed to the display leaf).
properties.config: appears in `.compose.yaml` as `type: dradis_contacts` with `center_x`/`center_y`/`radius`, `hud: true`, a `source: {namespace: dradis/contacts, default: "[]"}` block, and an `alert: {namespace: demo/alert}` block.
properties.change: "REMOVED ping-on-sweep-pass (beam/contact coupling): when the radar sweep beam passed over a contact it fired a ping cue. Deleted entirely — the `beam:` binding and the sweep-angle read go with it. The `sweep` widget still renders as the visual beam; it no longer drives any contact behavior."
context_for_change: prior_state: "The sweep beam was coupled to contacts: crossing a contact triggered a per-contact ping cue, computed each frame from the live sweep angle vs each contact's bearing."

reasoning: "On this tier the coupling fired inconsistently (angular sampling vs frame cadence made the crossing detection miss or double-fire) and the per-frame sweep-angle read against every contact cost real horsepower on a banded/framebuffer display that otherwise repaints only on bus change. The cue was decorative; the cost was structural (it defeated the event-driven publish-on-change repaint model by needing continuous per-frame evaluation)."

rejected_alternative: "Fix the sampling (sub-frame angular interpolation + hysteresis on the crossing) — rejected: it buys back a decorative cue by reintroducing an always-on per-frame compute loop, the exact thing the reactive tier's dirty-band/publish-on-change design exists to avoid ([CXC-ER-RENDER])."

invalidating_assumption: "That beam/contact coupling is not worth a continuous per-frame cost on this tier. If a future tier (Qualia framebuffer with idle headroom, or a design where the sweep cue is load-bearing rather than decorative) makes the per-frame budget free, reopen it — the visual `sweep` widget is still present to re-couple against."

implication: "The `sweep` widget is now purely visual; no contact behavior depends on the beam. Contact cues are driven only by bus state (alert) and widget-derived motion, both of which fit the publish-on-change model."

properties.definition: **`dradis/contacts`** is a JSON **array** of contact objects, published by any peer (scenario driver, an Intelligence, a sensor); the widget subscribes and re-renders on change. Fields per contact: `id` (stable string — the widget tracks a contact across updates by `id` so it can animate motion, not respawn); `type` (icon key → `bus://assets/icons/dradis/<type>.bmp`); `bearing` (degrees, **0 = up/12-o'clock, clockwise positive**); `range` (**physical distance in LIGHT-SECONDS**, float > 0); `allegiance` (`hostile`|`friendly`|`neutral` — drives tint + blink policy); `size` (optional px, default 72).
properties.alert-namespace: **`demo/alert`** — truthy ⇒ RED ALERT; hostile contacts blink while it holds ([CXC-ER-DRADIS-BLINK]). One bit; the temporal behavior is widget-owned.
properties.robustness: empty / `"[]"` source → no contacts, no crash; malformed JSON → warn-once + empty, never a hang.
properties.sensed-classification: `type` is the **currently SENSED classification, not necessarily ground truth** — the publisher owns the sensor model and may report `large_unknown`/`small_unknown` for an unresolved contact, republishing the **same `id`** so the icon morphs in place as it resolves ([CXC-ER-DRADIS-IDENT]; the sensor/identification model that owns identification + the threat-flip is the publishing application's sensor model, an app-layer concern). Full staged icon registry (all `bus://assets/icons/dradis/<type>.bmp`): `battlestar` (own-ship), `basestar`, `resurrection_ship`, `raider`, `raider_squadron`, `heavy_raider`, `viper`, `viper_squadron`, `raptor`, `civilian1`, `civilian2`, `civilian3`, `large_unknown`, `small_unknown`.
properties.change: "`range` semantics changed from a 0..1 normalized screen fraction to a PHYSICAL quantity — light-seconds (float > 0, typical 0.01…60) — rendered on a logarithmic scope ([CXC-ER-DRADIS-PROJ]); edge = 60 ls = 1 light-minute."
context_for_change: prior_state: "`range` was a 0..1 fraction: 0 = scope center, 1 = scope edge. The publisher pre-normalized distance to a screen position; the widget multiplied by the radius linearly."

reasoning: "That put a display concern (where on the glass) into the contract and made the number meaningless off this one scope — two scopes of different range spans could not share a contact array, and the publisher had to know the display's radius to place a contact. Making `range` a physical light-second distance moves the projection (including the log compression) entirely into the widget: the bus now states a real-world fact ('this contact is 12 light-seconds out'), and any scope renders it correctly at its own scale. It also unlocks a logarithmic scope, which a 0..1 fraction structurally cannot express."

rejected_alternative: "Keep 0..1 and add a separate `range_ls` field — rejected: two fields for one quantity, with the display-coupled one still authoritative for placement; the publisher would still be pre-normalizing to a screen fraction, which is the thing being removed."

invalidating_assumption: "That a radar contact's distance is a physical quantity the display projects, not a screen fraction the publisher pre-computes. If a consumer genuinely needs the publisher to own placement (e.g. a non-metric abstract scope with no physical range), that consumer wants a different widget, not this field overloaded back to a fraction."

implication: "Publishers emit real distances and are decoupled from any scope's geometry; the widget owns the linear-in-log₁₀ projection and the ring calibration. The scenario driver closes hostiles from ~60 ls toward ~1 ls over the timeline."

properties.definition: the scope is a **×60 light-clock** — total range 1 light-minute (60 ls), three concentric rings each a factor of 60, evenly spaced in radius. Radius is **linear in log₁₀(range_ls)**, anchored on the rings `(radius_px, range_ls) = (R/3, 1/60), (2R/3, 1), (R, 60)` (defaults R = 330 → 110/220/330).
properties.projection: `radius_px = clamp(220 + 61.86·log₁₀(range_ls), 0, R)` where `61.86 = 110 / log₁₀(60)`; `θ = bearing·π/180`; `x = center_x + radius_px·sin(θ)`; `y = center_y − radius_px·cos(θ)` (minus so bearing 0 points UP). Icon blitted centered at `(x, y)`, clipped to the scope circle.
properties.rings: three faint circles + labels — inner `1/60 LS` (~5,000 km) @ R/3, middle `1 LS` (~300,000 km) @ 2R/3, edge `1 LM` (60 ls) @ R. A contact nearer than 1/60 ls clamps toward center; beyond 60 ls clamps to the edge (or is dropped).

CXC-ER-DRADIS-MOTION.title: Directional Motion Indicator — the Decentralization Exemplar

properties.definition: every *moving* contact gets a directional pointer drawn BEHIND its sprite, rotated to point along its direction of motion. The heading is **NOT on the bus** — the widget DERIVES it locally: it already tracks each contact by stable `id`, keeps the previous projected `(x, y)`, and each update computes `heading = atan2(dy, dx)` from the **screen-space** delta (the visual motion the eye sees, already log-projected). Zero new contract fields.
properties.key-insight: this is the corpus's canonical exemplar of the decentralization principle — **complexity/derivation flows to the leaf; the bus carries only semantic position, never derivable mechanism.** The consumer already holds every input the heading needs (it holds the position stream by construction), so transmitting a heading would be transmitting a quantity the receiver can already reconstruct. The bus stays purely positional; the display reconstructs the motion.
properties.render-detail: the asset `directional_indicator.bmp` points DOWN by default (tip toward +y / 6-o'clock), so the applied rotation is `heading − (π/2)`. Render ONLY when motion exceeds a small epsilon (a still contact shows no vector); smooth the heading slightly so jitter doesn't spin it. Draw order per contact: indicator first, sprite on top.
properties.change: "Contact heading is DERIVED by the display widget from successive projected positions, NOT published on the bus. No `heading`/`course`/`velocity` field exists in the contract."
context_for_change: prior_state: "The natural first design adds a `heading` (or `course`) field to each contact so the widget can orient the motion indicator directly from the bus."

reasoning: "The consumer that draws the indicator already holds successive positions of the same contact (it tracks by stable `id` across updates, and it projects each position anyway). Heading is a pure function of those positions it already has — atan2 of the screen-space delta. Publishing it would put a derivable, redundant quantity on the bus, one that must be kept consistent with the positions it is derived from (a publisher could emit a heading that disagrees with the position delta). Deriving at the leaf makes inconsistency impossible and keeps the contract minimal and purely positional. Deriving in SCREEN space (post-log-projection) is also more correct for a motion indicator: it points along the visual motion the operator sees, which the log scope has already compressed — a bus-space heading would not match the on-glass vector."

rejected_alternative: "Publish a `heading` field computed by whoever moves the contact — rejected: redundant with position, a new consistency burden (heading-vs-position drift), and it would be a *bus-space* heading that disagrees with the log-projected on-screen motion the indicator actually depicts."

invalidating_assumption: "That the display holds the inputs to reconstruct the heading (the position stream, tracked by stable id). If a source ever emits a heading that is NOT derivable from the positions it publishes — e.g. a true instantaneous course from an inertial sensor that the sampled positions cannot recover — then that heading is genuine new information, not a derivable mechanism, and belongs on the bus as its own semantic field."

implication: "The contract carries no motion fields; any peer publishing only positions gets correct motion indicators for free. The same reasoning governs the derived HUD tally ([CXC-ER-DRADIS-HUD]) and the derived counts — the widget reconstructs, the bus does not transmit."

CXC-ER-DRADIS-BLINK.title: Blink on Alert — State on Bus, Behavior in Widget

properties.definition: `allegiance == "hostile"` AND `demo/alert` truthy ⇒ the contact blinks ~2 Hz. The alert state is ONE bit on the bus; the temporal blink (frame cadence, phase) lives entirely in the widget — animation frames are never streamed. This is [CXC-BIND-PRINCIPLE] (Problem 4) on the reactive tier: a peer flips one bit at intent altitude; the widget owns the presentation.

an optional small readout (`CONTACTS 4 · THREATS 2`), gated by `hud: true`, computed by the widget from the contact array — NOT a separate namespace. Threat count = hostiles; both counts are pure derivations of the array. Same leaf-derivation reasoning as the motion heading ([CXC-ER-DRADIS-MOTION]): the widget holds the array, so it reconstructs the tally rather than the bus transmitting it.

a **second bus namespace `dradis/bodies`** (distinct from `dradis/contacts`) — a JSON **array** of stellar objects (the "terrain": star / planet / asteroid), rendered by the same `dradis_contacts` widget UNDER the contacts (a backdrop layer). Fields per body: `id` (stable string), `kind` (`star`|`planet`|`asteroid`), `type` (icon key → `bus://assets/icons/stellar/<type>.bmp`), `name`, `bearing` (degrees, same convention as contacts), `range_ls` (**light-seconds**, same physical unit as a contact's `range`), `size` (optional px), plus room for later semantic props (stellar class / planet type / mass) that ride with the body so an Intelligence or a readout can reason about the system, not just draw it.
properties.projection-reuse: bodies project through the **same** log light-clock as contacts ([CXC-ER-DRADIS-PROJ]) on their `range_ls` — a body sweeps inward from the edge exactly as a contact does. The projection is body/contact-agnostic; only the field name differs (`range_ls` vs `range`).
properties.staged-assets: `planet_blue`, `planet_blue2`, `planet_dark`, `celestial_distant`, `asteroid_1..5`. Initial pass: **one star + one planet per system.**
properties.open-item-star-art: **no dedicated "star" art exists yet** — an open asset item for David; the initial star may borrow `celestial_distant`.
properties.constraint: the 350×350 stellar BMP32 assets are ~490 KB each — **over the 160 KB on-device image-fetch buffer.** Rendering bodies on the Qualia requires bumping the fetch/decode buffer (Qualia-only, as with the MQTT buffer) OR shipping a smaller on-device asset. A **build-time item, not a spec blocker** ([CXC-ER-RENDER]/R5 concern).

CXC-ER-DRADIS-IDENT.title: Fog-of-War Renders with ZERO Display Change — the Third Decentralization Exemplar

properties.definition: fog-of-war identification requires **no new display logic.** The display already maps `type → icon` and `allegiance → tint/blink`; the publisher reports `type` as the fleet's *currently sensed* classification and republishes the **same `id`** as a contact closes, so the icon **morphs in place** (`large_unknown` → the true type) and the "becomes a threat" flip is just a change to the existing `allegiance` bit. The widget grew nothing.
properties.key-insight: this is the **third** decentralization exemplar in this one widget — after the derived motion heading ([CXC-ER-DRADIS-MOTION]) and the derived counts/HUD ([CXC-ER-DRADIS-HUD]), which push *derivation* to the leaf, this one pushes *identification authority* to the publisher: the publishing application's sensor model (an app-layer concern) owns "what has been sensed / what is a threat", and the display consumes `type`/`allegiance` exactly as it always did. Identification is **published game state, not per-consumer re-derivation** — the display cannot recompute the true type from range (it is ground truth only the engine holds), so this is the *opposite* case from heading and correctly lives on the bus.
properties.contrast: unlike heading (a pure function of positions the display already holds, so bussing it would be redundant — [CXC-ER-DRADIS-MOTION]), the true type behind `large_unknown` is information the display does **not** hold; it is published, not derived.

CXC-CARTHING-INTENT.title: A Bought Surface That Proves the Input-HAL Story

The **DeskThing** community project reflashes it into a useful desk gadget that runs a webview + apps and exposes the hardware inputs.
